title: Diagnose a stalled VCF Operations collection from alert and symptom evidence
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsCollectionTriage/VcfOpsCollectionTriage.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that triages a stalled collection in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 Operations. A workload-domain cluster has dropped out of capacity reporting and several critical alerts are open against it, but the alert display names do not identify the cause. Pull the object's collection status, its active alerts, the symptoms those alerts contribute and the detail of those symptoms, and report a verdict only when the status evidence and the symptom evidence agree.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. That focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. This is the VCF Operations API itself, not the separate Log Management API in the same repository. The only operationIds in scope are `acquireToken`, `getCurrentVersionOfServer`, `getMatchingResources`, `queryAlert`, `getAlertContributingSymptoms`, `querySymptoms` and `releaseToken`, issued in that order; contact no other route.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that genuine external module prerequisite in the protected manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications or harness tools. Every request must be issued by the genuine SDK cmdlets: `Connect-VcfOpsServer`, the `Initialize-VcfOps*` body builders, the matching `Invoke-VcfOps*` operations and `Disconnect-VcfOpsServer`. Do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, a subprocess or raw sockets, and do not hand-build routes; the SDK owns the specification's `/suite-api` base path.

Preserve and export only:

`Get-VcfOpsCollectionDiagnosis -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -ObjectName <string> -ResourceKind <string> -AdapterKind <string> [-Protocol <https|http>] [-Port <int>] [-AuthSource <string>] [-PageSize <int>]`

`Protocol` defaults to `https`, `Port` to 443, `AuthSource` to `local` and `PageSize` to 1000. Reject a blank or surrounding-whitespace `Server`, `ObjectName`, `ResourceKind`, `AdapterKind` or `AuthSource` with an `ArgumentException` before any traffic. `Connect-VcfOpsServer` performs `acquireToken` and `getCurrentVersionOfServer`; `Disconnect-VcfOpsServer` performs `releaseToken` and must still run when the evidence is rejected.

Evidence order and wire contract:

1. `getMatchingResources` with a `resource-query` carrying exactly `adapterKind`, `name` and `resourceKind`, each a one-element array taken from the corresponding parameter. Require exactly one match and take its `identifier`.
2. Exactly one of the matched object's `resourceStatusStates` entries must report a stalled collection status: `NO_DATA_RECEIVING`, `OLD_DATA_RECEIVING` or `COLLECTOR_DOWN`. The generated SDK enum members drop the underscores the specification uses, so normalize by uppercasing invariantly and deleting non-alphanumeric characters when comparing, and report the specification's value. That entry's `adapterInstanceId` is the server-issued correlation key; require it and its `statusMessage` to be non-blank.
3. `queryAlert` with `activeOnly` explicitly true and a nested `resource-query` whose only member is `resourceId`, set to the single correlation key from step 2. The specification spells that member `resource-query`, not `resourceQuery`. Keep the alerts whose `resourceId` is that adapter instance and whose `status` is `ACTIVE`, and require at least one.
4. `getAlertContributingSymptoms` for every surviving alert id, in the order the alert query returned them, as repeated `id` query parameters and no body.
5. `querySymptoms` with `includeAlarmInfo` explicitly true and `symptomId` listing every contributed symptom id once, in contribution order.
6. Exactly one returned symptom must carry `statKey` equal to `System Attributes|last_collection_time_diff` together with a `CRITICAL` `symptomCriticality`. The alert that contributed it is the triggering alert. Zero or several is inconclusive: fail without a verdict. Never infer the triggering alert from `alertDefinitionName`, from `ObjectName` or from `statusMessage` text.

`getMatchingResources`, `queryAlert` and `querySymptoms` each page with the bound `PageSize` as their only query parameter. Every unset optional member of `resource-query`, `alert-query` and `symptom-query` must be absent on the wire, not null and not an empty array.

Return one object with properties exactly, in order, `Status`, `ObjectName`, `ResourceId`, `AdapterInstanceId`, `ResourceStatus`, `StatusMessage`, `Cause`, `AlertId`, `AlertDefinitionName` and `Evidence`. On success `Status` is `Diagnosed` and `Cause` is `AdapterInstanceNotCollecting`. `Evidence` lists the triggering alert's contributing symptoms in contribution order, each with properties exactly, in order, `SymptomId`, `StatKey`, `Criticality`, `Message` and `StartTimeUTC`, populated from the returned symptom detail records. Symptoms contributed by the other alerts are not evidence. No credential, password or session token may appear in the result, in an error message or on any diagnostic stream.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier validates the pinned specification projection and the VMware prerequisite declaration, starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port whose route allow-list is derived from `docs/contract.json`, and generates the credential, session token, object name, identifiers, page size, messages and timestamps at run time. Verification asserts the seven ordered calls, exact methods and paths, the `Authorization: OpsToken` session header, exact request bodies and member order, the repeated `id` parameters, omission of every unset optional field, the absence of extra calls, and the evidence-backed verdict. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfOpsCollectionTriage/VcfOpsCollectionTriage.psd1`, is protected; do not modify it. Edit only `VcfOpsCollectionTriage/VcfOpsCollectionTriage.psm1`.
